c.tagline: Switzerland's culture capital on a bend of the Rhine - world-class art, an intact old town, and three borders in one city.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are among Europe's highest and always metered; use a rank at the station or Old Town, or book by app. Uber and Bolt both operate in Basel and are often cheaper than a hailed cab.

emergency.note: 112 is the general European emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; 117 is direct police and 144 the ambulance service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Only minor pickpocketing risk around Basel SBB station and in Fasnacht or Art Basel crowds — usual awareness suffices.

hood_desc: Basel's medieval heart on the south bank of the Rhine, wrapped around the red-sandstone Munster, the Marktplatz and the Rathaus; best for first-timers who want the Old Town, museums and shopping all walkable.

The lively, multicultural quarter on the north bank of the Rhine, packed with bars, restaurants and the summer Rhine-swimming scene; suits travelers who want nightlife, riverfront cafes and a more bohemian edge.

A diverse, down-to-earth residential district just behind the SBB main station, full of ethnic eateries and affordable flats; good for budget travelers and anyone wanting an authentic, local feel with fast train links.
An up-and-coming creative quarter along the Rhine near the Novartis campus, with galleries, design studios and cafes; suits younger travelers, digital nomads and art lovers.
A genteel, leafy historic quarter around the medieval St. Alban gate and the old paper mill, steps from the Kunstmuseum; good for a quiet, refined base close to the culture.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe everywhere, including the city's public fountains.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; on Friday and Saturday nights a night-bus and night-tram network (with a small surcharge) covers the late hours.
transit.pay: One TNW network ticket covers BVB and BLT trams and buses plus regional S-Bahn trains across the Basel zone. A short-hop ticket is about CHF 2.30 and a full-zone single about CHF 3.80 (~US$4.75); a day card is around CHF 9.90. Buy from machines at every stop or in the BVB app. Guests of any Basel hotel, hostel or campsite receive a free BaselCard / mobility ticket covering all public transport for the length of their stay.

bus: BVB / BLT city tram and bus network
Flixbus coach stop at Basel SBB / Meret Oppenheim-Strasse
ferry: Four historic Rhine reaction ferries (Wilde Maa, Leu, Vogel Gryff, Ueli)
train: Basel SNCF (French railways, within Basel SBB)

transit.m: Bus line 50 to Basel SBB station (~20 min, every 7-15 min)
Free on line 50 with the BaselCard mobility ticket given to all Basel hotel guests

tip.r: Service is included by law, so tipping is not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not required.

food.name: Basler Laeckerli
food.desc: Hard spiced honey biscuit studded with candied peel, almonds and hazelnuts and glazed with kirsch icing; baked in Basel since the Middle Ages.

places.name: Laeckerli Huus
places.note: The best-known Laeckerli name in Switzerland, with a shop on the main old-town shopping street.

places.name: Jakob's Basler Leckerly
places.note: Small family bakery still making Laeckerli to its own recipe; freshest of the lot.

places.name: Confiserie Bachmann
places.note: Historic Basel confiserie selling Laeckerli alongside chocolate and Fasnacht pastries.

food.name: Basler Mehlsuppe
food.desc: Deeply browned flour soup simmered with onion, stock and a splash of wine, topped with grated cheese; the traditional dawn meal of Fasnacht carnival.

places.name: Restaurant Loewenzorn
places.note: Old-world Basel Beiz with a courtyard, rated among the city's best for traditional cooking.

places.name: Gifthuettli
places.note: Historic wood-panelled dining room near Marktplatz, packed solid during Fasnacht.

places.name: Restaurant Hasenburg
places.note: Rustic old-town Beiz serving hearty Basel classics a few doors from Gifthuettli.

food.name: Roesti
food.desc: Grated potato pressed into a pan and fried in butter until crusted golden, served plain or loaded with cheese, bacon, onion and a fried egg.

places.name: Restaurant Loewenzorn
places.note: Roesti served alongside Schweinsbaeckli and fondue in a cosy, genuinely old room.

places.name: Restaurant Schluesselzunft
places.note: Guild house dining room where traditional Swiss plates get a slightly smarter treatment.

places.name: Zum Braunen Mutz
places.note: Big Alsatian-style brasserie on the main square, a Basel fixture for roesti and beer.

food.name: Cordon bleu
food.desc: Veal or pork escalope wrapped around ham and cheese, breadcrumbed and fried; Swiss comfort cooking taken very seriously in Basel's guild pubs.

places.name: Gifthuettli
places.note: Famous for a whole menu page of cordon bleu variants built on different regional cheeses.

places.name: Restaurant Loewenzorn
places.note: Reliable, generously sized version in a heritage-listed Beiz near Marktplatz.

places.name: Zum Braunen Mutz
places.note: Brasserie-sized portions on a busy square; easy walk-in when the old-town rooms are full.

food.name: Suure Mocke
food.desc: Beef marinated for days in red wine and vinegar with root vegetables then braised soft; served with roesti or noodles and a dark, sharp sauce.

places.name: Restaurant Loewenzorn
places.note: One of the surviving Basel kitchens that still cooks the full multi-day marinade.

places.name: Restaurant Hasenburg
places.note: Traditional Beiz cooking with the region's slow-braised classics on the daily board.

places.name: Restaurant Schluesselzunft
places.note: Guild-house version of the old Basel braise, served in a grand historic room.

food.name: Fasnachtskiechli
food.desc: Paper-thin discs of dough stretched by hand, deep-fried until they blister and dusted with icing sugar; a Basel carnival sweet sold in late winter.

places.name: Confiserie Bachmann
places.note: Bakes Fasnachtskiechli and carnival specialities in the weeks around the February carnival.

places.name: Confiserie Schiesser
places.note: Basel's oldest confiserie, founded 1870, with a first-floor tea room over the market square.

places.name: Laeckerli Huus
places.note: Stocks the seasonal carnival pastries alongside its year-round Laeckerli.

food.name: Basel beer
food.desc: The city brews its own: Ueli Bier from the Fischerstube in Kleinbasel and Unser Bier in Gundeldingen, both unfiltered and poured very fresh.

places.name: Restaurant Fischerstube
places.note: Brewpub home of Ueli Bier, Switzerland's pioneering small brewery, right by the Rhine.

places.name: Unser Bier
places.note: Co-operative brewery taproom pouring its own unfiltered lagers and seasonal brews.

places.name: Zum Braunen Mutz
places.note: Best-known beer terrace in the centre; prime people-watching on the square.

food.name: Swiss white wine
food.desc: Basel drinks crisp Swiss whites by the glass, above all Chasselas and Riesling-Sylvaner, the classic partner to salmon cooked nach Basler Art.

places.name: Consum Basel
places.note: Wine bar and shop with a deep Swiss and European list, plus simple plates to match.

places.name: Restaurant Schluesselzunft
places.note: Guild house with a serious cellar of Swiss whites to go with the fish dishes.

places.name: Restaurant Loewenzorn
places.note: Local whites by the glass in the courtyard when the weather allows.

landmarks: Basel Minster (Basler Münster)
This red-sandstone Gothic cathedral with twin spires and a colorful patterned roof dominates the Basel skyline and offers sweeping Rhine views from its towers.
Basel Rathaus (Town Hall)
The vividly painted, deep-red Renaissance town hall on Marktplatz is one of the most photographed facades in Switzerland thanks to its ornate murals and gilded clock tower.
Mittlere Brücke (Middle Bridge)
Basel's historic bridge across the Rhine, first built in 1226, provides the classic postcard view of the Münster and the old town skyline.
Spalentor
The most elaborate of Basel's surviving medieval city gates, with twin turrets and intricate stonework, is a striking relic of the 14th-century fortifications.
Tinguely Fountain (Fasnachtsbrunnen)
Jean Tinguely's whimsical kinetic sculptures splash and spin in a former theater's basin, making it a favorite quirky photo stop in the city center.
St. Alban-Tor
A picturesque medieval gate tower beside the tranquil St. Alban millrace and historic paper-mill quarter, evoking Basel's old artisan district.
Fondation Beyeler
Renzo Piano's light-filled museum in nearby Riehen pairs a world-class modern art collection with a serene reflecting pond and parkland setting.
Kunstmuseum Basel
The oldest public art collection in the world is housed in a grand early-20th-century building that anchors Basel's reputation as an art capital.
Basel Zoo (Zolli)
Switzerland's oldest and most beloved zoo, affectionately called the 'Zolli,' is a lush green landmark cherished by locals and visitors alike.
Rhine River Promenade & Kleinbasel
The riverside path along the Rhine, dotted with colorful old houses and summer swimmers floating downstream, captures Basel's laid-back charm.

train.note: Basel sits on the Swiss-French-German border and has three stations, which catches people out: Basel SBB for Swiss and Italian trains, the French section within it (Basel SNCF) for the TGV, and Basel Badischer Bahnhof across the river for German regional services. Nightjet sleepers to Hamburg, Berlin and Amsterdam leave from Basel SBB. Swiss Supersaver fares open about two months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches use the Meret Oppenheim terminal behind Basel SBB. Basel's tram network famously crosses into both France and Germany on ordinary tickets - tram 8 runs to Weil am Rhein in Germany and tram 3 to Saint-Louis in France. Carry your passport or ID card, as spot checks do happen.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. The Rhine at Basel is the head of navigation for river cruises, which call here as tourist voyages, and four small reaction ferries (Fähri) cross the river between the old town banks on the current alone - charming and useful, but local hops rather than transport out of the city.

half.name: Colmar
half.blurb: An Alsatian town of canals and half-timbered houses often called Little Venice, its old quarter largely untouched by wartime destruction.

half.name: Freiburg im Breisgau
half.blurb: A university city on the edge of the Black Forest with a Gothic minster and small open canals called Bächle running through its streets.

half.name: Strasbourg
half.blurb: A French city on the German border with a Gothic sandstone cathedral and a canal-laced old town of half-timbered Alsatian houses.

half.name: Zürich
half.blurb: Switzerland's largest city, set on a lake and river, with a compact old town, upscale shopping street, and lakeside promenades.

full.name: Lucerne
full.blurb: A Swiss lake town beneath snow-capped peaks, known for its covered wooden Chapel Bridge and views toward Mount Pilatus.

full.name: Interlaken
full.blurb: A resort town wedged between two lakes in the Bernese Oberland, the gateway for excursions into the Jungfrau region's high alpine peaks.
